results.title: Re-verify the #14 fixes on a full applied frame
results.requirement: The contrast, type-size and spacing fixes, verified on a complete applied frame rather than on the compiler output alone.
results.knownIssue:
PASS on 16 Oct 2026. Earlier in the session this was carried as an open failure because the hosted `create_design` timed out mid-transaction and committed a partial frame. It was latency, not an operation cap: the same 52-operation program later committed 32 operations before the client gave up, and re-issuing the compiler's own remaining operations in two smaller transactions completed the frame. A 17-operation and a 5-operation transaction both returned `success` with no timeout.

The frame is 57 nodes across three transactions, all from `compile_ir` output with only the parent references rewritten from transaction-local ids to the real Figma ids the previous transaction returned — the documented way to build across several calls, not a hand-written substitute.

Measured on the complete frame (node 317:414, applied at x=18000 on page Branding):

    nav label       #A8ABA0 on the #111111 rail   8.09:1   (was 3.82:1)
    device memory   11px                                 (was 10px)
    pill padding    4px top and bottom                  (was 2px)

review_design on all 57 nodes returns one finding, off-grid-geometry (minor). The four rules #14 touched — text-contrast, tiny-technical-text, off-scale-spacing and text-outside-autolayout — all report zero, where the pre-fix frame reported text-contrast and tiny-technical-text as serious and text-outside-autolayout 20 times.

The render also surfaced three defects the reviewer did not, recorded as L05, L06 and L07. This case closes; those three stay open.
results.detail: Complete 57-node frame applied and reviewed. Nav label 8.09:1 on the rail (was 3.82:1), device memory 11px (was 10px), pill padding 4px (was 2px). Review returns 1 minor finding; all four rules #14 touched report zero.

results.title: The active nav item's label takes the same fill as its own background
results.requirement: A navItem with state 'active' paints its pill in the accent fill and must paint its label in a colour that reads against that fill.
results.knownIssue:
Label and pill are the same colour, so the active item's label is invisible.

Measured on the applied frame: node 317:420 (the active pill) and 317:421 (its label) render as the same yellow. Rendering each node in isolation shows the glyphs in the accent fill on a white canvas, and the pill as solid accent. Contrast 1.0:1 against a 4.5:1 requirement.

The #14 fix made nav labels follow their surface via onDarkSurface(), which is right for the three inactive items on the dark rail and wrong for the active one: the active item's surface is the accent pill, not the rail. The rule keys on the rail, not on the node the label actually sits in.

review_design reported no text-contrast finding on the 57-node frame that contains this. Either the rule resolves the wrong ancestor for a nav label, or it skips labels whose parent is a component instance. Either way a 1.0:1 pair is being reported as clean, which is the more serious of the two halves.
results.detail: Active nav label fill equals the active pill fill (contrast 1.0:1); review_design reports 0 text-contrast findings on the frame that contains it.

raw.evidence: isolated renders of both nodes are the same accent yellow

results.title: A region with width 'fill' ignores the sibling occupying the left edge
results.requirement: A region declared { width: 'fill', right: <inspector width> } must be laid out in the space left after the other regions, not from x=0.
results.knownIssue:
Topology is placed at x=0 with width 1120, while the 220px nav rail occupies x=0..220. The region is therefore underneath the rail, and its contents are occluded.

The compiler's own trace agrees with itself here — this is not the verifier inventing a position. compile_ir emits setPosition x=0 and setSize width=1120 for node 317:418, and the applied frame matches the emitted geometry exactly. The fill width is canvasWidth - right, with no accounting for a region already placed at the left edge.

The render shows all three device nodes (mac-mini-01, mac-pro-02, rack-07) drawn inside the dark rail at x=24. They are children of Topology and their coordinates are correct relative to it; the region itself is simply underneath Nav.

review_design reported no occlusion or overlap finding. overflow only checks a region against its parent's bounds, and a region that is fully inside the frame cannot overflow it — so this class of error is invisible to the current rules.
results.detail: Topology (317:418) is placed at x=0 width=1120 and is fully occluded by the 220px nav rail for its first 220px; three device nodes are buried under it. No review rule covers region-vs-region occlusion.
